get.description:
Returns a paginated page of this tenant's audit log entries, newest first, resolved against
the current catalog and the principal cache: `resource.displayName` prefers a resource's
current title over the snapshot recorded at write time, `resource.exists` says whether it
still does, and `caller` is resolved the same way an item revision's author is.

Entries recording a read of the audit log itself are excluded unless `includeAuditLogReads`
is set — otherwise a console that pages or refreshes the log would fill its own first page
with records of itself. This is a view default, not a recording decision: those entries are
written and reachable with the one query parameter regardless.

`occurredSince`/`occurredUntil` default to no bound; narrowing the window is what keeps a page
cheap regardless of how large the table has grown. `skip` beyond 10 000 is rejected — narrow
the filters instead of paging deeper.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: How many matching entries to skip before this page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of entries to return.

parameters.name: occurredSince
parameters.description: Return only entries recorded at or after this instant.

parameters.name: occurredUntil
parameters.description: Return only entries recorded strictly before this instant.

oneOf.description:
Whether the call succeeded or failed. Stored verbatim in `audit_log.outcome` despite being

`Deserialize` unconditionally: also what `GET /audit-log`'s `outcome` query parameter accepts.

which otherwise share the same kind, uid and urn.

`Deserialize` unconditionally, not just under `#[cfg(test)]`: this is also what `GET
/audit-log`'s `scope` query parameter accepts, matching `as_sql_str`'s spelling exactly.

get.summary: List the principals of a tenant
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of the principals — people and machine identities — registered in the tenant carried by the ACL context.

The request is carried out on behalf of the caller, so it returns what that caller is allowed to see, and a refusal by the identity service — `403` when they may not list principals at all, for instance — reaches them under its own status and with its own message. It fails with `502` when that service is unreachable, fails with a `5xx`, or is not configured at all.

oneOf.description:
Whether a principal is a person or a machine.

The distinction is worth returning rather than leaving a client to infer from the display name:
the two are rendered differently (an avatar versus a service badge), and "who changed this"
reads very differently when the answer is an automation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Return only the principals named by this comma-separated list of identifiers, at most 200 of

It exists so a client holding a saved filter — a set of identifiers, with no names — can
turn it back into something displayable in one request. An identifier naming no principal is
simply absent from the response rather than an error, since a filter kept across a
principal's removal is the ordinary case.

get.description:
Returns all items that have a relationship with the specified catalog item, together with
the relationship records themselves.

Each entry in the response carries:
- `direction`: whether the queried item is the `source` (`outbound`) or the `target`
  (`inbound`) of the relationship.
- `relationship`: the full Relationship item (always full — required for direction and
  type-grouping logic).
- `relatedItem`: the item on the other end of the relationship, if resolvable. The shape
  depends on the `Accept` header: full item for `application/json`;
  `PartialObjectMetadata` for `application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata`.

The response can be grouped by relationship direction **or** type using the `groupBy`
query parameter. The two values are mutually exclusive.

Supports content negotiation via the `Accept` header for the `relatedItem` field.
- `application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata`: `relatedItem` contains only metadata.
- `application/json`: `relatedItem` contains the full item.
Missing or wildcard `Accept` header values default to the full item response.

An optional `rawq` parameter may be supplied to filter entries by properties of the
`relatedItem`. Predicates are expressed in the Catalog query language as URL-safe
base64-encoded JSON objects. Multiple values are combined in *AND*. When active,
entries whose resolved `relatedItem` does not satisfy the predicates are excluded from
the response.

An optional `direction` parameter (`inbound` or `outbound`) restricts the response to
entries of a single direction. Both `rawq` and `direction` may be combined freely.

Every filter is applied before the results are paginated, so a page always carries as many
matching entries as `limit` allows: a short page means the end of the results has been reached,
and a `continue` token is only ever returned alongside a full one.

The response only ever contains related items the caller is allowed to read. The route itself is
authorized against the *subject* item's type, but the items on the other end of a relationship
can be of any type, so the authorization policy additionally forwards the caller's readable item
types as an `acl-filter` query parameter. Entries whose related item is excluded by it are
dropped from the response entirely, rather than returned without `relatedItem`: the relationship
record carries the other end's URN, which would otherwise disclose an item the caller may not
read. The parameter is an internal contract between the policy and this service and is therefore
deliberately not documented as a parameter of this operation.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description:
Groups the response entries by the specified dimension.

Accepted values: `direction`, `type`. The two values are **mutually exclusive**;
providing both in the same request returns `400 Bad Request`.

*Example*: `?groupBy=direction`

parameters.name: rawq
parameters.description:
A selector to filter the `relatedItem` field of each relationship entry.

Queries are expressed as JSON objects in the Catalog-specific query language, encoded
as URL-safe base64 strings. Multiple `rawq` values are chained in *AND*.

When one or more `rawq` values are supplied, only entries whose resolved `relatedItem`
satisfies **all** predicates are returned. Entries whose related item is not resolvable
from the `items` table are also excluded when `rawq` is active.

Filterable fields:
- `metadata.name`, `metadata.title`, `metadata.tags`, `metadata.urn`,
  `metadata.labels.*`, `apiVersion`, `kind`
- any `spec.*` field (no type-level validation — related items may be of any kind)

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description:
Restricts the response to entries of the specified direction only.

- `inbound`:  only entries where the queried item is the *target* of the relationship.
- `outbound`: only entries where the queried item is the *source* of the relationship.

Omitting the parameter returns entries of both directions (the default behaviour).

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description:
Specifies the desired response format. Supported values are:
- `application/json` (equivalent to `application/*`, `*/*`, or an absent `Accept` header) for a full object response,
- `application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata` for a partial response that includes only metadata.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of items. The list can be filtered and sorted using query parameters.

Supports content negotiation via the `Accept` header.
- `application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata`: returns a partial representation of the items without the `spec`.
- `application/json`: returns the full items.
Missing or wildcard `Accept` header values (i.e., `*/*` or `application/*`) will default to the full items response.

The list items API does not include the following "core" Catalog items:
- Relationships
- Relationship Types
- Relationship Constraints
- Custom Fields

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return.

parameters.name: continue
parameters.description: The server-generated token to retrieve more results in a paginated request.

parameters.name: rawq
parameters.description:
Queries made with the `rawq` are expressed as JSON objects written in a Catalog-specific query language.
They must be sent in the URL as [URL-safe base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64#url_and_filename_safe_base64) encoded strings.
Multiple `rawq` parameters can be specified, and they are chained in *AND* with each other and with the other filtering query parameters.

Fields that can be queried include:

- `apiVersion`
- `kind`
- `metadata.name`
- `metadata.labels`
- `metadata.title`
- `metadata.tags`
- `metadata.owner`
- any selectable field in `spec`

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The field by which results should be sorted.

The default sorting order is ascending lexicographical order.
If the field name is prefixed by a `-`, then descending lexicographical order will be applied.

Specifying the query parameter multiple times means that the results will be sorted for multiple fields, with the sort order evaluated from the first-appearing query parameter to the last.

Sorting can be performed on:

- `metadata.creationTimestamp`
- `metadata.updateTimestamp`
- `metadata.name`
- `metadata.title`

*Example* : -metadata.name

put.summary: Create or update an Item Type Definition
put.description:
Creates a new Item Type Definition or updates an existing one. The match is made based on the `metadata.name` field.

When providing the body, ensure that:

- the `metadata.name` field matches the `name` path parameter, and
- the `resourceVersion` field is provided for updates and matches the current resource version of the Item Type Definition stored in the system.

If the request resolves to an update, and the body contains modifications to read-only fields (e.g., `spec.group`), those modifications will be ignored, and a `Warning` header will be added to the response.

`spec.history` is applied **only when this request creates** the Item Type Definition. | Call | Effect | Versions |

exists.description:

family.description:
The plural family segment of an item-kind resource's own URL

The owning Item Type Definition's display plural (e.g. "Widgets"), falling back to its

timestamp.description: When the caller acted — the request's start time, not when the row was written.

miaplatform.eu.v1.AuditOutcome.description:
Whether the call succeeded or failed. Stored verbatim in `audit_log.outcome` despite being
derivable from `status_code`, so a query for partial failures has a small dedicated index
rather than a filter evaluated row by row — see the table's own comment.

`Deserialize` unconditionally: also what `GET /audit-log`'s `outcome` query parameter accepts.

miaplatform.eu.v1.AuditResourceKind.description:
The sort of thing an action acts on. Stored verbatim in `audit_log.resource_kind`.

Deliberately carries no notion of one-versus-many — that is [`ResourceScope`]'s job, so that
listing a family and reading one item of it file the same `resource_kind` and are still told
apart by scope alone.

miaplatform.eu.v1.AuditResourceScope.description:
The granularity an action acts at. Stored verbatim in `audit_log.resource_scope`, and returned
verbatim as `resource.scope` on the consultation API — it is what tells a collection-scoped
listing of a family apart from an instance-scoped read of that family's Item Type Definition,

`Deserialize` unconditionally, not just under `#[cfg(test)]`: this is also what `GET

enableRead.description: Whether read operations on the items of the defined type are recorded in the audit log. Write operations are recorded whenever the tenant has auditing enabled, regardless of this setting.

metadata.description: A validation on the `metadata.name` property to apply specific restrictions.

spec.description: A validation on the `spec` property of the items.

miaplatform.eu.v1.NewWebhook.description:
The request body of the create-webhook operation.

`uid` and `createdBy` are server-set and are deliberately not accepted here: a webhook is created
under an identifier this service issues, attributed to whoever the request carries.

`enabled` *is* accepted, and defaults to `true`. Passing `false` creates a subscription that is
paused from the start — configured, listed, and delivered nothing until it is switched on.

`secret` is optional. A subscription created without one delivers unsigned, and says so through
`hasSecret` on every read of it.

description.description: A free-text note on what the webhook is for, for a human reading a list of them. It is not interpreted by the service and is never delivered.
examples: Feeds the pipeline that reconciles deployments after a repository changes

enabled.description: Whether deliveries are made at all. Defaults to `true`. Pass `false` to create the webhook paused: it is stored and returned by the read operations like any other, and nothing is delivered to it until it is switched on with a patch.

name.description: A label for the webhook, for a human reading a list of them. It does not have to be unique and it is not an identifier.

onCreate.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is created.

onDelete.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is deleted.

onUpdate.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is updated.

secret.description:
The shared secret every delivery to this webhook is signed with, as an `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC-SHA256 header over the raw request body. It is write-only: it is accepted here and on a patch, and is never returned by any read operation — `hasSecret` is how a read says whether one is set.

Optional. Omitting it, or passing `null`, creates a subscription whose deliveries are **unsigned**: they carry no signature header, and a consumer of one has no way to tell a real delivery from anything else that can reach its URL. A key can be added later with a patch.

It must not be blank, must be at most 512 characters, and must not begin or end with whitespace. That last one is a rejection rather than a trim: the key is stored and signed with byte-exactly as supplied, so silently trimming it would change the key without telling anyone, on the one field no read can hand back for comparison.

url.description: The address to deliver the event to. It must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL. Redirects are never followed at delivery time, so it must be the final address.

miaplatform.eu.v1.WebhookPatch.description:
The request body of the patch-webhook operation.

It follows [JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7396) semantics: a key
that is absent leaves its current value unchanged. `name`, `description` and `secret` are the
fields that can be *cleared* with an explicit `null`, because they are the ones a subscription is
allowed not to have — a `null` `url`, `enabled` or `on…` flag names no state a webhook can be in,
and is refused rather than silently coerced.

description.description: The new note on what the webhook is for, or `null` to clear it.
examples: Feeds the pipeline that reconciles deployments after a repository changes

enabled.description: Whether deliveries are made. Setting it to `false` pauses the webhook without discarding its configuration; it keeps appearing in the read operations either way.

name.description: The new label of the webhook, or `null` to clear it.

onCreate.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is created.

onDelete.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is deleted.

onUpdate.description: Whether to deliver when an item of this type is updated.

secret.description:
The new shared secret to sign deliveries with, or `null` to remove the one there is. Supplying a value rotates the key: the next delivery is signed with it, and the previous one is not recoverable. Omitting the field leaves the current key — and the record of when it was last changed — untouched.

Removing the key leaves the subscription delivering **unsigned**, the same state a create that carried no secret produces. `hasSecret` on the response is the answer either way.

url.description: The new address to deliver the event to. It must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL.
